% Converted, ltx-talk. C-FRAME-OPT workaround: name the key. The mapping is total and
% unambiguous, so convert_deck.py applies it: b -> vertical-alignment=bottom,
% t -> top, c -> center, allowframebreaks -> auto-break=true.
%
% auto-break=true, not auto-break: it is the missing '=' that gets a list thrown away,
% not the unknown word. Measured on 0.6.0, one over-long frame -- [auto-break] gives 2
% pages (the key never fired), [auto-break=true] gives 1.
%
% Measured placement of the body text, lualatex, 0.6.0, pdftotext -bbox yMin:
%   no option / [b] / [t]      135.76   <- all three identical: centred
%   [vertical-alignment=bottom] 247.96
%   [vertical-alignment=top]     23.57
% So the fixture pair compiles either way and the suite cannot catch this one; the
% yMin measurement is the check that can.
%
% Not fixable in the preamble: defining b/t/c as real keys in talk/frame leaves [b] centred
% anyway, because the list is never parsed. And this file will NOT build under beamer --
% "! Package keyval Error: vertical-alignment undefined". Both are in the catalogue entry,
% with the four-line beamer-side shim for decks that must build both ways.
%
% plain, shrink, squeeze, noframenumbering have no ltx-talk key at all. fragile is
% moot: verbatim goes through frame* (C-VERBATIM), not through a frame option.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[vertical-alignment=bottom]
\frametitle{Pinned to the bottom}
This paragraph sits at the foot of the slide, under the empty space.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
